answers.M8-S1: The author got stung many times and hurt about half the bees while marking them with chalk, but two bees still came home with pollen.
answers.M8-S2: To show how strong the wind was, so the bees had to fly really close to the ground and couldn't fly high.
answers.M8-S3: They stopped to collect pollen from flowers on the way, so they weren't just rushing home; they had time to eat and gather food.
answers.M8-S4: So he could tell which bees were his when they came back to the nest, since Aglaé was watching for them.
answers.M8-S5: At first he doubted the bees would make it home because of the wind and injuries, but then he was surprised and excited when Aglaé said two had arrived.
answers.M8-S6: It goes in time order, telling the steps of the experiment from catching the bees to them getting home.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast the bees flew, two and a half miles in less than forty-five minutes, even while stopping to get pollen.
answers.M8-S8: To show that marking bees was hard and painful, he kept getting stung and squeezed them too hard by accident.
answers.M8-S9: That they couldn't see landmarks from above, so they had to find their way home some other way, which is impressive.
